subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document a supported split-host public `wss://` mobile pairing pattern where browser/operator access stays behind SSO/OIDC while a separate mobile hostname uses OpenClaw token plus setup-code device bootstrap auth?
rationale: This would define a public Gateway exposure boundary and explain when mobile setup-code bootstrap may bypass browser-style HTTP identity redirects, so automation should not choose the supported security posture.

options.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
options.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while covering a dedicated mobile `wss://` hostname, token/device bootstrap auth, `trustedProxies`, origin settings, and validation steps.

options.title: Keep Existing Generic Guidance
options.body: Leave docs focused on Tailscale Serve, trusted-proxy auth, and general exposure warnings, treating public split-host mobile pairing as operator-managed advanced setup.

options.title: Defer Public Mobile Pairing Direction
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide whether public mobile pairing beyond Tailscale Serve is a first-class supported deployment shape.

recommendation.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while covering a dedicated mobile `wss://` hostname, token/device bootstrap auth, `trustedProxies`, origin settings, and validation steps.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent Tailnet route-list fix and adjacent iOS pairing/security docs history make this the strongest available owner signal for the public mobile pairing trust-boundary decision.
